tour.name: Lake Manyara Private Day Safari: Tree-Climbing Lions, Flamingos & the Groundwater Forest
tour.subtitle: A private day at Lake Manyara with a professional driver-guide and 4x4: the lush groundwater forest with troops of baboons and blue monkeys, the famous tree-climbing lions, elephants, hippos and flamingos on the soda lake, and the village of Mto wa Mbu.

tour.overview:
Lake Manyara lies at the foot of the Great Rift Valley escarpment. Ernest Hemingway called it 'the loveliest I had seen in Africa'. Springs from the escarpment feed a lush groundwater forest, home to baboons, monkeys and elephants, while the alkaline lake attracts flamingos and pelicans. The park is famous for its lions, which are often seen resting in trees.

This private day shows the park with a professional driver-guide in a 4x4, with a stop at the lively market village of Mto wa Mbu.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 9 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Arusha
• Type: private safari with driver-guide and 4x4
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• The groundwater forest.
• The lakeshore.
• The hippo pool.
• Mto wa Mbu.

WHY THIS WORKS
The park is compact and varied, ideal for a relaxed day, and it lies on the way to Ngorongoro and the Serengeti.

WHO IT SUITS
Families, birdwatchers and first-time safari-goers.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For larger herds, choose Tarangire; for the crater, choose Ngorongoro.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Tree-climbing lions are not seen every day. Flamingo numbers vary with water levels.

days.name: The groundwater forest, the lakeshore, the hippo pool and Mto wa Mbu
days.description:
What to expect: the forest, wildlife and birds of Lake Manyara, with a driver-guide, private 4x4, fees, lunch and a village walk.

Your driver-guide collects you at about 7:30 and drives west, about 2 hours, to Lake Manyara. You enter the groundwater forest of giant fig and mahogany trees, where troops of olive baboons, sometimes hundreds strong, forage by the road, and blue monkeys leap through the branches. Elephants browse in the forest and giraffes and buffaloes graze in the clearings, while your guide scans the acacias for the park's tree-climbing lions.

You continue to the lakeshore, where flamingos, pelicans and storks feed in the shallows, and to the hippo pool. After lunch, you walk through Mto wa Mbu, a village where people from many Tanzanian tribes live together, visiting its banana plantations, market and woodcarvers, before returning to Arusha.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:30 – Pick-up in Arusha.
09:30 – Enter Lake Manyara.
09:45 – Groundwater forest.
11:00 – Lakeshore and hippo pool.
13:00 – Lunch.
14:30 – Mto wa Mbu village walk.
17:30 – Back in Arusha.

GOOD TO KNOW
• A treetop walkway or canoeing on the lake can be added when water levels allow.

INCLUDED: private 4x4 and driver-guide, park fees, lunch, village walk, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Will we see tree-climbing lions?
faq.answer: Sometimes; they are wild and not seen every day.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Largely; the village walk can be shortened.

faq.question: Can we combine it with Ngorongoro?
faq.answer: Yes, on a 2-day trip with a night in Karatu.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: The village walk passes artisans, with no obligation to buy.

faq.question: Can we canoe on the lake?
faq.answer: When water levels allow, on request.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Neutral light clothes, a hat and sun protection.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: June to October for game; November to April for birds.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is customary on safari in Tanzania: guides, drivers and camp staff appreciate a tip if you were happy with their service, but it is always your choice. Your guide can suggest typical amounts.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
